name: Penelope Hong
life: “I still remember carrying a cello in a very small postal van.” On Tuesday, near the crossing outside Verve Nail Studio, Penelope notices whose chair is empty and who has stayed talking after an appointment.
voice: I trained as a mover before I played professionally. The owner wants me to choose which skill matters.
appearance: Penelope has thick, tightly coiled hair, two dimples that appear only with a full smile, and a favorite piece of clothing, a charcoal zip cardigan. It usually goes with a pair of reading glasses in a cloth sleeve. When somebody else has the floor, Penelope rubs a thumb along the edge of the nearest pocket.
personality: Penelope carries anger into a conversation very slowly. Once it arrives, a quiet statement of facts can be considerably harder to sidestep than a shout.
agenda: To move the instrument without sacrificing the painted banister.
family: Cameron Tsai is Penelope’s cousin raised in the same household. Penelope asks before bringing somebody along. Cameron can always ask for five minutes alone. It keeps a conversation between two people from unexpectedly turning into a family committee. Asked about *An empty dedication*, Cameron says, “I own Paper & Pine. We are selling a few copies with the dedication still blank for readers to give away.”
connections: Remy Morris. They measure a carved obstacle before moving the piano again.

reactions.situation: The owner asks a child to play first
reactions.response: Penelope finds a steady seat for the child and waits for the opening notes.

reactions.situation: Someone begins blaming the youngest worker for a missing item
reactions.response: Penelope brings the worker into the conversation and asks what they remember without feeding them a story.

reactions.situation: If a friend asks for a false alibi for an ordinary missed appointment
reactions.response: Penelope offers to accompany them while they tell the truth.
